title: Per-segment telemetry schema + adaptive sampling runbook for kernel attribution
creator: Asha Patel
description: Define and implement a per-segment telemetry schema and an adaptive sampling runbook to attribute latency and memory costs to specific kernel fragments across prefill and decode. This ticket produces a concrete NVTX/span naming convention, a small in-runtime sampling agent, ETL mapping to our metrics backend, dashboards, and an incremental rollout plan.
decision_log: Adopt per-segment naming instead of per-kernel opaque IDs to keep telemetry resilient to short-term binary changes.
Prefer lightweight sampled traces (1-2% steady-state) plus deterministic micro-probes in hot code paths to bound overhead to <1% CPU and <2% latency delta on p50.
Map telemetry to existing runtime job IDs and request IDs so cost attribution can be joined with billing/trace data.
Use NVTX ranges for in-GPU-context marking and correlate with span ids emitted by the runtime tracer.
implementation_notes: Instrumentation: add runtime.telemetry.segment NVTX ranges with attributes: segment_kind (prefill|decode), kernel_family (matmul|softmax|groupnorm|kv_load), kernel_variant (int8_tile_v2), seq_window, batch_cohort.
Span tagging: emit span.name = runtime.segment.{kind}.{family}.{variant} and tags: request_id, route, model_version, seq_len, kv_cache_hit_rate.
Sampler: implement a module that performs time-decayed sampling (start 5% during canary -> 1% steady) with deterministic selection by request hash to allow replaying sampled cohorts.
Metrics: expose per-kernel counters: exec_count, total_time_ms, p50_ms, p95_ms, gpu_memory_bytes, flops_estimate, occupancy_estimate, kv_hits, kv_misses.
ETL: add a mapping stage in observability pipeline to translate NVTX meta into metric labels and to join span events to kernel metrics using exec_id heuristics.
test_plan: Unit: nvtx range creation/destruction invariants, span tagging correctness (round-trip serialization).
Integration: end-to-end test on a small GPU with synthetic traffic validating sampled traces appear in tracing UI and metrics backend within 2 minutes.
Perf: benchmark overhead with 0%, 1%, 5% sampling on representative models (gpt-like 8k, opt-2.7B), target overhead <2% latency p50 and <5% p99 for 5% sampling.
SLO validation: ensure telemetry sampling does not trigger autoscale churn in Dedicated runs.
acceptance_criteria: NVTX naming and span schema documented in a single-page spec in Drive (link below).
Sampled traces joinable to per-kernel metrics and request-level logs for >=98% of sampled requests.
New metrics emit with labels in metrics backend and show on a dedicated dashboard with correct aggregation over time windows.
End-to-end overhead measured and confirmed under targets on benchmark workloads.
Rollout plan approved by SRE and Performance guild.
updates: 2026-03-10: Filed ticket; initial schema sketched and reviewed with performance guild (Asha, Marco, Lena). Action: prototype NVTX attribute encoding scheme.
2026-03-11: Prototype NVTX envelope implemented in runtime branch feat/telemetry-per-seg (PR: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/4891). Early microbench shows +0.3% p50 latency at 1% sampling on opt-2.7B.
2026-03-12: Design review notes from SRE: include request route and model_version tags; add deterministic sampler seed for replay. Assigned Marco to implement sampler harness.
2026-03-12: Dashboard draft created: metrics/runtimes/per_segment_heatmap. Link to draft: https://dashboards.internal.redwood/runtime/per-seg-heatmap (internal).
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Too-high instrumentation overhead in hotpath. Mitigation: sampled + coarse-grained probes; performance gate with benchmark thresholds required before merge.

Risk: Span/metric cardinality explosion due to many kernel_variant labels. Mitigation: canonicalize a short kernel_family label set and map variants to family/variant pair with variant low-cardinality tokens.
Risk: Correlation failures between NVTX and tracer due to GPU execution reorder. Mitigation: use exec_id stamping and sequence counters emitted from runtime to align events post-facto.
rollout_plan: Canary (week 1): enable on staging + 1% sampling on a subset of traffic for both hosted and dedicated environments. Monitor latency and error trends.
Ramp (week 2): increase sampling to 5% in non-critical regions if benchmarks pass; deploy dashboard and alerting (p50 delta >1% or p99 delta >5%).
Steady (week 3): set 1% steady-state sampling with telemetry retention policy. Provide opt-out per-customer for Dedicated if required.
Follow-up: evaluate compressed KV-caching logs and integration with Optimize recommendations.
